statement: For every finite simple tree T on exactly 21 vertices, every zero of its independence polynomial I(T,z) has strictly negative real part. Hence every such polynomial is stable in the frozen source's closed-left-half-plane sense. The exhaustive census contains exactly 2,144,505 unlabeled isomorphism classes; each has a regular exact Routh table with strictly positive first column, and there are no unstable or singular classes.
contribution: A complete computer-assisted exact resolution of the frozen order-21 question, strengthening its non-strict conclusion to strict Hurwitz stability. The contribution advances the cited prior computational boundary from order 20 to order 21, with a collision-free canonical census, integer tree-DP coefficients, exact Routh certificates, and a differently implemented systematic audit; it does not claim a general characterization or unqualified literature priority.
